subject: bicycle maintenance
note: A deliberately small, neutral registry. The point of this repository is the routing and quality machinery, not the domain content.

claims.statement: Replace the chain once elongation reaches 0.5% on an 11- or 12-speed drivetrain; waiting until 0.75% usually means replacing the cassette as well.
Skipping only under load, with clean indexing at rest, points to a worn cassette rather than to cable tension.
Wax-based lubricants are widely reported to extend chain life relative to wet lubricants in dry conditions, but published comparisons vary in method and the size of the effect is disputed.
claims.source: Independent lubricant test programmes, methods not harmonised

claims.statement: Pads contaminated with oil cannot be reliably cleaned; replace them and clean the rotor with isopropyl alcohol.
A lever that firms up after several pumps indicates air in a hydraulic system and calls for a bleed.
Straightening a warped rotor by hand is widely practised and sometimes effective, but it is not a specified repair and results are inconsistent.
Correct pressure is a function of rider plus bike mass, tyre width and surface; it cannot be given as a single number without those inputs.
claims.source: Tyre pressure models published by tyre manufacturers

claims.statement: Tubeless sealant dries out and needs topping up on a schedule that depends on climate and casing porosity.
Lower pressure is often described as universally faster; in practice there is an optimum below which rolling resistance rises again.
Saddle height set from inseam gives a starting point only; final height is confirmed by observed knee angle at the bottom of the stroke.
Persistent numbness is a fit and pressure-distribution problem, not a saddle-padding problem, and softer saddles frequently make it worse.
Range is capacity divided by average consumption; consumption depends on assist level, gradient, mass and wind, so a range figure without those assumptions is not meaningful.
Lithium packs stored for long periods keep capacity better at a partial state of charge than at full or empty.
Suspected carbon damage is assessed by ultrasound or tap testing; visual inspection alone does not clear a frame after an impact.
A creak reported as coming from the bottom bracket originates elsewhere often enough that the diagnostic sequence should not start there.
Fasteners on carbon interfaces are torqued to the component maker's figure with a calibrated wrench; feel is not an acceptable substitute.
